# Naim Montazeri, Ph.D.

## Microbial Food Safety | Virology | Predictive Modeling | Risk Assessment

I am a microbial food safety scientist with over 15 years of experience in applied microbiology, virology, sanitation validation, and predictive modeling. My work focuses on understanding how pathogens persist, transfer, and are inactivated across foods, agricultural systems, and environmental surfaces to support science-based product development, process validation, and risk-based decision-making.

My research integrates experimental microbiology with quantitative data analysis and predictive modeling to translate laboratory findings into practical food safety solutions. Areas of expertise include sanitation validation, environmental monitoring, agricultural water safety, thermal process validation, microbial persistence, and quantitative microbial risk assessment.

My experience spans academia, industry collaboration, and regulatory science, bridging microbiology, product and process development, and data-driven decision making to support consumer safety, product performance, and public health.
:::

## Experience Snapshot

- Assistant Professor, University of Florida (2018–2026)
- Postdoctoral Researcher, North Carolina State University (2015–2018)
- Research Assistant, Louisiana State University (2012–2015)
- Research Assistant, University of Alaska Fairbanks (2009–2011)

## Core Areas of Expertise

- Virology, applied microbiology, and pathogen control
- Sanitation validation and disinfectant efficacy
- Predictive microbiology and quantitative modeling using R
- Environmental monitoring and contamination control
- Agricultural water safety and preventive controls
- Thermal process validation and microbial inactivation
- Quantitative microbial risk assessment (QMRA)

## Research and Technical Portfolio

My research integrates experimental microbiology, predictive modeling, and risk assessment to address practical challenges in food safety, sanitation, and pathogen control. Across laboratory, pilot-scale, and field studies, I develop science-based approaches that support product development, process validation, environmental monitoring, and evidence-based food safety decisions.
